Package org.aeonbits.owner

Interface Mutable

All Superinterfaces:
Config, Serializable
public interface Mutable extends Config

Allows a Config object to change its property values at runtime.

Example:

     public interface MyConfig extends Config, Mutable {
         @DefaultValue("18")
         int minAge();
     }

     public void example() {
         MyConfig cfg = ConfigFactory.create(MyConfig.class);
         int before = cfg.minAge();                 // before = 18
         int old = cfg.setProperty("minAge", "21"); // old = 18
         int after = cfg.minAge();                  // after = 21
         int old2 = cfg.removeProperty("minAge");   // old2 = 21
         int end = cfg.minAge();                    // end = 18 (falls back to the default value)
     }
Since:
1.0.4

    • setProperty

      String setProperty(String key, String value)

      Sets a given property to the specified value.

      Differently than Properties.setProperty(String, String), if key is set to null then this call is equivalent to removeProperty(String).

      Parameters:
      key - the key to be placed into the property list.
      value - the value corresponding to key, or null if the property must be removed.
      Returns:
      the previous value of the specified key, or null if it did not have one.
      Since:
      1.0.4

    • loadFromXML

      void loadFromXML(InputStream inStream) throws IOException
      Reads a property list from an XML document, the way this library reads one from a source and not the way Properties.loadFromXML(InputStream) does.

      The two differ on what counts as a document. Properties reads the format its own DTD defines - <entry key="a">b</entry> - and refuses everything else. This reads that format and any other XML, flattening the tree into keys the same way the XML loader does when the document is named in @Sources, so that a file which can be a source can also be handed to this method. That is what #62 asked for in 2013.

      Everything else is as load(InputStream): the properties are merged into the ones already held, the listeners are told, and a transactional listener may refuse the change.

      The stream is closed when this returns, which load(InputStream) does not do to its own. The asymmetry is the JDK's and is followed rather than corrected: Properties.load(InputStream) leaves the stream open and Properties.loadFromXML(InputStream) closes it, so a caller who knows one of those two already knows this one. Verified against the JDK rather than assumed.

      The document is validated against the grammar it declares, if it declares one. The option that turns that off is written on a source - file:app.xml#validate=false - and a stream is not a source, so a document that breaks its own DTD has to be named as one to be read here.

      Parameters:
      inStream - the input stream, closed when this returns.
      Throws:
      IOException - if an error occurred when reading from the input stream, or the document is not well formed, or it breaks the grammar it declares.
      Since:
      2.0.0
      See Also:
      • Properties.loadFromXML(InputStream)
